content: Spouses married September 1994 under community property, acquired apartment in Palermo, separated January 1997. Wife sought division requesting various remedies including in-kind division, assignment, or auction sale. Husband appeared November 2013 (after twenty-day deadline) claiming exclusive payment of purchase/renovation costs under Article 1115(3), requesting increased share. Articles 167(2), 720, 1115(3) Italian Code of Civil Procedure and Civil Code govern filing deadlines, indivisible property division, and share increases for improvements. The issue concerned defendant's late-filed counterclaim admissibility and proper division method. Article 167(2) forfeiture regarding counterclaims is absolute, mandatory, detectable ex officio, relates to procedural public policy—independent of parties' will. Defendant's November 2013 appearance (post-deadline) forfeited right to file counterclaims and strict-sense objections. Article 1115(3) claim (share increase for improvements) constitutes counterclaim aimed at right ascertainment and share expansion—subject to counterclaim preclusions, declared inadmissible as untimely brought. Separation approval dissolved legal community, transforming property into ordinary joint ownership with each spouse entitled to assert dissolution rights per Articles 713 et seq. applicable via Article 1116. Court-appointed expert deemed property indivisible: load-bearing masonry prevents substantial modifications; division would create portions too modest (approximately 43 and 38 sqm net) for residential function, unsuitable for independent enjoyment, significantly depreciated. Article 720 applies: preferential criterion (assignment to larger shareholder with excess charge) inapplicable—neither party validly requested assignment. Plaintiff requested assignment to husband; husband requested sale. Auction sale ordered, proceeds divided 50-50. Property valued €75,000.00 by expert, valuation approved by parties. Costs fully compensated given defendant's acceptance and party relationship. Expert costs borne equally.
